title: Staged hosted endpoints PRD: scope clarifications, gated acceptance, and launch sentry
creator: Sana Patel
description: A focused PRD to clarify minimal and stretch scope for hosted API endpoints (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank), define per-endpoint acceptance gates, and provide an operational launch sentry checklist for a staged rollout. This doc resolves outstanding scope drift from earlier drafts and codifies telemetry and eval gating required for go/no-go at each canary step.
background: Multiple PRDs exist for unified hosted endpoints but stakeholders reported ambiguity in the minimal feature set vs. launch stretch items. Customer trials require clear quality and performance guarantees plus runbook items for degraded fallbacks. This ticket consolidates decisions and produces an acceptance-oriented checklist for PM/Eng/Design to sign off.
scope_inclusions: Behavioral contract: deterministic stop handling, consistent top-k rerank ordering under identical inputs
Operational guardrails: per-tenant rate limiting, token-level cost telemetry, rollout canary hooks
Compatibility: Redwood SDKs (node/python/go) basic parity for request shapes and streaming semantics
Eval harness: baseline prompt/quality test sets for each endpoint integrated into CI
scope_exclusions: Advanced multimodal attachments (image/audio) for initial launch
Enterprise-only RBAC UIs and tenant management features (deferred to Private launch)
Full interactive conversation lineage UI in Console (analytics only)
success_metrics: Quality: no significant regression vs. baseline eval (>95% of golden prompts within tolerance)
Reliability: P99 request success >= 99.5% during canary and >= 99.0% at GA
Performance: median token latency targets met per-profile (see performance_targets)
Cost: per-token unit cost within projected budget for initial traffic profile
Adoption: automated smoke tests and >= 90% of staging customer testcases passing
acceptance_criteria: API contract validated: integration tests pass for request shapes, streaming, function-calling stubs
Quality evals: endpoint-specific evals (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank) show no more than 5% delta against reference baseline on key metrics
Performance gating: canary cluster meets p50/p95/p99 latency thresholds and throughput targets under synthetic traffic
Fallbacks: automated fallback to compatible model variant verified (functional and monitored)
Telemetry & alerts: dashboards instrumented with token-level cost, model variant breakdown, error budgets, and runbook links
Security: KMS integration smoke test and basic audit logging verified in hosted environment
Docs and SDKs: public API reference + quickstart compiled and smoke-tested with sample apps
api_contract_summary: Chat: message array input, streaming SSE/HTTP2 streaming, supports function calling metadata (JSON schema) in initial surface
Completions: prompt/temperature/top_p/stop sequences; streaming optional; max_tokens default 2048 for GA
Embeddings: single vector per input text; dimension and model id appear in response; batching supported
Rerank: accepts candidate list and query, returns stable top_k with scores and tie-breaking deterministic seed
performance_targets: Chat median token generation latency (hosted-default model): p50 < 90ms per token, p95 < 350ms per token under nominal load
Completions end-to-end latency for short prompts (<=64 tokens): p50 < 120ms, p95 < 400ms
Throughput: canary cluster should sustain 1k qps synthetic with <5% increase in error rate vs baseline
rollout_plan: Stage 0 - Internal smoke: internal test accounts, 0.1% of production traffic, run 72h
Stage 1 - Partner canary: 1% traffic from invited pilot customers, 48h, monitor quality regressions and cost
Stage 2 - Gradual ramp: increment traffic 1% -> 10% over 7 days, apply automated rollback if error budget breached
Stage 3 - Regional expansion: enable EU/APAC regions after regional telemetry validation
Stage 4 - GA: open sign-ups with post-launch 14-day monitoring and a rollback window
launch_checklist: Merge gating: all blocking PRs merged and CI green (see links)
Eval gates: automated eval pass threshold met for each endpoint
Telemetry: live dashboards deployed with alert thresholds (error rate, latency, cost per token)
SLOs and SLO burn alerts configured and tested
Runbooks: incident runbook published and on-call informed
Fallback verification: test route to fallback model and ensure metrics emitted
API docs: public reference + example apps in SDKs validated
Support readiness: KB article, escalation contact, and postmortem template in Drive
Legal/compliance: security sign-off recorded and KMS audit trail verified
Billing: token accounting verified on test tenants and billing reports validated
risks_mitigations: Risk: Quality regressions introduced by model variant selection. Mitigation: eval-driven rollout and automatic rollback based on eval-probe fail rate.
Risk: Token cost overruns during ramp. Mitigation: per-tenant spend alerts and conservative default batching/quantization profiles.
Risk: Incomplete SDK parity. Mitigation: ship minimal examples for node/python and mark advanced features as beta with clear compatibility notes.
Risk: Regional compliance delays. Mitigation: delay region expansion until KMS/audit verification completed; keep staged timeline flexible.
